We introduce CORE-Bench (Computational Reproducibility Agent Benchmark), a benchmark consisting of 270 tasks based on 90 scientific papers across three disciplines (computer science, social science, and medicine). Tasks in CORE-Bench consist of three difficulty levels and include both language-only and vision-language tasks. We provide an evaluation system to measure the accuracy of agents in a fast and parallelizable way, saving days of evaluation time for each run compared to a sequential implementation. We evaluated two baseline agents: the general-purpose AutoGPT and a task-specific agent called CORE-Agent. We tested both variants using two underlying language models: GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini. The best agent achieved an accuracy of 21% on the hardest task, showing the vast scope for improvement in automating routine scientific tasks. Having agents that can reproduce existing work is a necessary step towards building agents that can conduct novel research and could verify and improve the performance of other research agents. We hope that CORE-Bench can improve the state of reproducibility and spur the development of future research agents.

. Our work makes three contributions. Fi.zh: . Our work makes three contributions. First, we develop benchmark adapters that port more than 80 benchmarks to evaluate arbitrary agents, and validate them through rigorous code review and parity experiments. Second, we conduct a large-scale evaluation of 8 models spanning capability tiers across 54 benchmarks; every model is run with Terminus-2 and with one of 3 native harnesses. This enables a broader analysis of agent capabilities and failure modes than was previously possible. Third, we introduce Harbor-Index, a curated set of 82 difficult, diverse, and high-quality tasks spanning 29 benchmarks, refined from the adapted suite through difficulty filtering, AI and human audit, and an audit-and-fix loop. Harbor-Index preserves the challenge and breadth of large-scale agentic evaluations while being affordable to run; no evaluated model-harness configuration exceeds 30% pass rate, and the strongest (GPT-5.5 with Codex) reaches 28.0%. We release the adapters, evaluation results, in-depth analysis, and Harbor-Index as open-source artifacts to support more reliable and comprehensive evaluation of language-model agents.

, a benchmark suite for agentic inferenc.zh: , a benchmark suite for agentic inference. It uses real traces from agentic benchmarks, such as SWE-Bench and TerminalBench, alongside standard chat baselines. This enables benchmarking of models on multi-turn tasks involving tool calling, skill utilization, and increasing context lengths. AgentPerfBench also samples from empirical distributions of input length, output length, and turn count derived from the real traces, generating representative synthetic profiles for cheap and accurate measurements on new hardware. In addition, we further find that several existing benchmarks fail to accurately reflect real hardware performance for two key reasons: 1) they do not account for realistic context-length growth, and 2) they measure inference performance without operating at hardware saturation. We discuss these issues in detail and provide rich kernel-level Nsight Compute (NCU) traces to construct a new multi-dimensional roofline model that captures hardware-system limitations in both memory bandwidth and memory capacity footprint. The benchmarking suite then includes automated scripts to identify potential bottleneck conditions on emerging hardware when evaluated with diverse agentic traces. Together, these contributions quantify the chat-to-agentic gap in current inference benchmarks and characterise per-kernel GPU resource utilisation via roofline analysis.

through a controlled full-factorial eval.zh: through a controlled full-factorial evaluation of six open-source harnesses and three lightweight coding models across 100 SWE-bench Verified tasks, producing 1,800 graded runs under common serving, metering, and grading conditions. For the same model, resolution rates differ by up to 44 percentage points across harnesses, while harness rankings change across models. We apply an evidence-based failure taxonomy to 1,100 unsuccessful runs and find substantial differences in failure patterns across harness-model pairings. A model's dominant failure modes under one harness need not dominate under another. Efficiency is similarly dependent on the pairing: even among model-directed loop harnesses, charged tokens per resolved task vary by more than 20-fold. These findings make harness-model selection a central deployment decision for lightweight coding agents. Strong performance with one harness or model does not guarantee similar results with another. We translate these findings into practitioner guidance for pairing selection, token-efficiency assessment, and trajectory-informed harness engineering, and release the complete experimental records and analysis artifacts.

Evaluating four modern LLMs (GPT 4.1 mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite, Qwen-3.5-35B-A3B, and Llama 3.1 8B Instruct), we expose model-specific vulnerability profiles invisible to outcome-only evaluation; Qwen-3.5-35B-A3B, for example, leads on tracer durability and instruction stability, while GPT 4.1 mini leads on leakage containment and false-belief resistance. Across 360 controlled runs over ten software workloads and three models, Relic raises complete-contract delivery from 14.06% to 19.76% (+5.71 percentage points) over a matched structured team without the protocol lifecycle, improving all four verified production endpoints in every model stratum. Supervisors can subscribe to the event stream; when forking is needed, the system copies the Agent's state along with the sandbox environment to a new branch, keeping the original branch, and continues from the specified location. This allows local retries or comparison with another operation without having to restart the task from the beginning each time. Irreversible external side effects still go beyond the guarantee of a recoverable environment.

The supervisor observes the trajectories of both and can take three actions: inject guidance into a worker; let the lagging side fork from the state of the leading side and resume; or terminate a stuck worker. The first is for lightweight reminders, while the latter two change the actual execution state. The original text also demonstrates workflow local replay optimization and trajectory forking during training.

. Given a task specification, benchmark.zh: . Given a task specification, benchmark examples, and a seed pipeline, DeCAF identifies relevant optimization dimensions and generates diverse experimental hypotheses for each. Independent coding-agent sessions then optimize each dimension under a restricted edit scope, jointly evaluating performance, inference cost, and latency while recording all hypotheses, edits, and outcomes of each experiment. A final synthesis session combines compatible findings across all dimensions and uses a component-level trajectory evaluator, which derives role-specific rubrics from each agent’s instructions, to localize underperforming components and guide cross-dimension revisions. Across a diverse suite of agentic benchmarks, DeCAF improves average task performance by 2.58 percentage points, while reducing inference cost by 4.30% and end-to-end latency by 42.45% compared to the best overall baseline.

管理者先建立工作依赖图，只有前置实现已经完成并合入主分支的任务才可委派。联系紧密.en: The manager first establishes a work dependency graph, and only tasks whose prerequisites have been completed and merged into the main branch can be assigned. Files with close connections or circular dependencies are preferably assigned to the same engineer. Each engineer develops, runs checks, and submits code in an independent git worktree (isolated working directory in the same repository). After a task is completed, the manager integrates the changes, updates dependencies, and assigns the next task to an available engineer.

AgentPrune 先把边的开关放松为可优化的权重，在少量交互轮次中采样通信结.en: AgentPrune first relaxes the edges to optimizable weights, samples the communication structure over a few interaction rounds, adjusts the weights based on final problem-solving quality, and adds constraints to encourage structural simplification. Then, a portion of the connections is pruned at once according to the weights, and remaining rounds pass messages only along the retained connections. In this way, a member does not have to read all outputs from everyone in each round.

方法为各轮建立独立的通信权重，先采样结构、运行任务，根据任务得分优化轮内连接；再.en: The method establishes independent communication weights for each round, first samples the structure, runs the task, and optimizes intra-round connections based on task scores; then, based on the weighted connections of the nodes, removes participants with low contribution in that round along with their related edges. After completing the participant reduction, intra-round and cross-round connections are re-optimized, continuing to prune unimportant message channels. What is optimized are the parameters of the communication graph; it is not necessary to update the weights of the task model for this.

论文先观察生产轨迹，再用 AutoGen 移植内部编码助手和 Deep Rese.en: The paper first observes production trajectories, then uses AutoGen to port the internal coding assistant and Deep Research Agent, constructing experimental workloads based on SWE-bench Pro and Deep Research Bench respectively. In cluster experiments, the original frontier model roles were mapped to 3B–14B Qwen and Llama series, but the specific mapping was not disclosed. The prototype modifies SGLang's routing, scheduling, and hierarchical caching, and is measured on 8 A100 80GB GPUs. The authors report that at peak concurrency, average job completion time is reduced to about 1/1.38–1/2.90 of the baseline, and output throughput is 1.12–1.96×. This evidence pertains to service performance; the paper does not verify corresponding changes in software repair pass rates or research report quality. Highly dynamic workflows with unpredictable historical paths may also reduce the benefit of advance preparation.

编排层把角色调用顺序表示成 Agent Step Graph。每次请求携带当前角.en: The orchestration layer represents the sequence of role invocations as an Agent Step Graph. Each request carries the current role and the steps remaining until each role's next invocation. The inference service uses these steps to update KV cache nodes corresponding to fixed prompts, and when GPU memory is tight, it prioritizes clearing cache that is less likely to be reused soon. When several roles share a prefix node, the service also considers which role might use it earliest.

The scheduler temporarily skips requests whose cache is still being transferred and executes requests that are ready first. Here, the already computed KV of the same prefix is reused.
